title: Faraday Future Unveils $2,490 Nova and $299 Nova Mini Humanoid Robots
key_facts: FF EAI Robotics and Faraday Future Intelligent Electric announced on 15 Oct 2026 two humanoid robots: FF Nova at $2,490 and FF Nova Mini at $299.
The companies call Nova America's first embodied-AI humanoid priced below $2,500; this is their own claim.
Nova stands 49.7 cm tall, weighs 2.8 kg, has 20 degrees of freedom and walks at 0.1 metres per second, or rides a wheeled base at 0.8 metres per second.
Nova Mini is a $299 teaching humanoid with a $499 curriculum; a Nova developer skills package costs $390.
Phase One is an invitation-only run of 100 Nova units, the first 20 ready for delivery; applications run for seven days at developer.ff.com.
Phase Two opens to all developers and schools; the full consumer launch is Phase Three.
The developer programme is based on Nvidia's Isaac platform, with a ROS 2 workflow and an open SDK.
quote_evidence: FF Nova is being released in three phases.
Phase One is a limited, invitation-only run of 100 units for invited developers and educational institutions, with the first 20 units ready for immediate delivery.
It can walk, turn, wave, and return to its feet after being knocked over.
why_it_matters_hint: Humanoid hardware is being priced for hobbyists, schools and developers, not only factories.
notes: Read from Unite.AI, which relays the companies' announcement; specifications come from the product page cited in the article. "America's first" is the companies' claim.
